faqs.question: What is Arium Advance EDI used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Type 2 pure water system used for microbiological media and reagent preparation, chemical analysis and synthesis solutions, histology, ELISA and RIA, buffer and pH solution preparation, and feeding laboratory instruments.

faqs.question: What water quality does Arium Advance EDI produce?
faqs.answer: Type 2 pure water with a resistivity of 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently at rates up to 10 L/h.

faqs.question: What is electrodeionization and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: EDI removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than a depleting exchange capacity, which is what allows water quality to stay consistent instead of declining across a service interval.

faqs.question: What contaminants does the system remove?
faqs.answer: Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the potable feed water, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield.

faqs.question: Does Arium Advance EDI produce Type 1 ultrapure water?
faqs.answer: No. It produces Type 2 pure water. Where Type 1 is also needed, this system can feed a downstream ultrapure polisher, or a combined system covering both grades may be the better fit.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-function display responds to a light touch through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?
faqs.answer: Three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so it fits the space actually available rather than requiring space to be cleared.

faqs.question: Does it extend the life of downstream systems?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with consistent Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

faqs.question: What production rates are available?
faqs.answer: 5 L/h and 10 L/h, depending on the configuration selected.

faqs.question: What is the price of Arium Advance EDI in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the production rate and installation format required.

longForm.heroHook: 5 to 15 MΩ·cm, held steady. No resin swap, no purity drift between services.
longForm.heroLead: Cartridge-based deionizers start strong and decline. Resistivity drops as the resin exhausts, and the water feeding a media prep or an autoclave in week six isn't the water that fed it in week one — which is exactly the kind of variable that quietly undermines reproducibility. Arium Advance EDI works differently. Patented electrodeionization runs continuously, holding Type 2 pure water at 5 to 15 MΩ·cm at production rates up to 10 L/h, connected straight to the potable feed. Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates come out reliably, with the highest ion retention rates alongside optimum purified water yield. iJust software reads the actual feed water condition and adapts to it, tuning water usage and calculating cleaning cycles rather than running fixed intervals. Purified water then sits in the closed arium® bagtank, protected from the airborne contamination an open reservoir invites.

body.text: Arium Advance EDI connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces Type 2 pure water at rates up to 10 L/h.
Resistivity holds between 5 and 15 MΩ·cm, delivered consistently rather than declining across a service interval.
Proprietary, patented electrodeionization sits at the core, achieving the highest ion retention rates while maintaining an optimum yield of purified water.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are reliably removed from the incoming feed water.
iJust software makes the best use of the initial feed water condition specifically, adapting to what's actually coming in rather than assuming a fixed input quality.
The same software enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage compared with conventional systems, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects it from secondary contamination between production and point of use.
The touch-function display responds through gloves, with structured menu navigation that removes guesswork from routine operation.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits the space the lab has rather than requiring space to be made.
Feeding downstream ultrapure water systems with this Type 2 water gives them a guaranteed longer service life.

sections.eyebrow: Continuous EDI and Consistent Water Quality
sections.title: Continuous EDI and Consistent Water Quality

items: Electrodeionization removes ions continuously using an electrical field rather than depleting a fixed pool of exchange capacity, which is why purity holds instead of declining as a cartridge would.
That continuity is what makes 5 to 15 MΩ·cm a working range rather than a peak figure — the water produced late in a service interval matches the water produced early in it.
The highest ion retention rates come alongside an optimum yield of purified water, so purity isn't achieved by rejecting an unreasonable proportion of the feed.
Oxidants, heavy metal ions, and particulates are all removed reliably, covering the contaminant classes that most commonly compromise media preparation and analytical solution work.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed with this water get a guaranteed longer life, because their own polishing consumables aren't compensating for an inconsistent input.
The closed bagtank protects that consistency after production — quality achieved at the membrane isn't given back to airborne contamination in an open storage vessel.

body: Feed water quality isn't uniform. It varies by site, by season, and sometimes by day, and a system that assumes a fixed input either over-treats or under-performs.
iJust makes the best use of the initial feed water conditions specifically, adapting operation to what's actually arriving rather than to an assumed baseline.
Cleaning cycles are calculated from that real condition instead of running to a fixed timer, so the system cleans when it needs to and not on a schedule that ignores it.
Water usage drops compared with conventional systems, which matters directly wherever feed water is metered, restricted, or carries real cost.
Purified water quality improves alongside that economy — iJust enhances quality rather than trading purity for lower consumption.
The touch-function display keeps all of it accessible: a light touch works through gloves, and structured menu navigation means routine control doesn't require interpreting the system.

faqs.question: What is Arium Advance RO used for?
faqs.answer: It's a Type 3 reverse osmosis water system used to supply feed water to ultrapure water systems, rinse glassware and laboratory vessels, and feed instruments such as autoclaves, glassware dishwashers, and humidifiers.

faqs.question: What water grade does Arium Advance RO produce?
faqs.answer: Type 3 reverse osmosis water, with the highest ion retention in its class at rates up to 24 L/h.

faqs.question: What flow rates are available?
faqs.answer: Constant flow rates of 8, 16, and 24 L/h, selected to match actual daily demand.

faqs.question: What is automatic membrane backflushing?
faqs.answer: The system periodically reverses flow across the RO membrane using purified water, lifting accumulated fouling off the surface without any operator step or service visit.

faqs.question: Why does backflushing use purified water rather than feed water?
faqs.answer: Cleaning with purified water avoids reintroducing the salts, particulates, and organics the membrane is there to remove in the first place.

faqs.question: How is Arium Advance RO different from Arium Advance EDI?
faqs.answer: RO produces Type 3 water at 8 to 24 L/h for feed, rinsing, and instrument supply. EDI produces Type 2 water at 5 to 15 MΩ·cm up to 10 L/h for media, reagent, and analytical solution preparation.

faqs.question: Can Arium Advance RO feed an ultrapure water system?
faqs.answer: Yes. Supplying downstream ultrapure systems is a primary application, and consistent Type 3 feed gives them a guaranteed longer working life.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it makes the best use of available water resources, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-function display responds to a light touch through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?

body.text: Arium Advance RO connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces Type 3 reverse osmosis water of the highest quality.
Constant flow rates of 8, 16, and 24 L/h are available, so output is chosen against actual demand rather than fixed at a single rate.
Ion retention is the highest in its class at rates up to 24 L/h, meaning volume doesn't come at the cost of retention performance.
Automatic RO membrane backflushing runs with purified water, clearing the membrane surface without manual intervention or a service call.
iJust software makes the best use of available water resources, enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, protecting it from secondary contamination between production and point of use.
The touch-function display responds through gloves, with clearly structured menu navigation that takes guesswork out of routine control.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits into the space the lab already has.
Downstream ultrapure water systems fed from this supply get a guaranteed longer service life, since consistent input is what determines how hard their consumables work.

sections.title: Automatic Backflushing and Membrane Life
sections.tabSummary: What self-cleaning membranes change day to day

items: RO membranes foul. Rejected salts, particulates, and organics accumulate on the membrane surface, and left alone that layer reduces both flux and retention performance over time.
Arium Advance RO backflushes the membrane automatically using purified water, reversing flow to lift that accumulation off the surface before it consolidates.
Because the backflush uses purified water rather than raw feed, the cleaning step doesn't reintroduce the contaminants it's meant to be removing.
Automatic means it happens on the system's schedule, not the lab's — no operator step, no reminder, no dependence on someone remembering during a busy week.
The practical result is retention performance held closer to specification across the membrane's life, and a membrane that reaches its replacement point later rather than sooner.
iJust sits alongside it, calculating optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition rather than running fixed intervals that ignore what's really happening at the membrane.

sections.eyebrow: Constant Flow Rates and System Flexibility
sections.title: Constant Flow Rates and System Flexibility

cards.title: Output matched to actual daily volume
cards.description: Choice of 8, 16, or 24 L/h constant flow rates

body: Under-sizing a Type 3 system turns it into a bottleneck: glassware waits, autoclaves wait, and the downstream ultrapure polisher runs short. Over-sizing pays for capacity that never gets used.
Three constant flow rates — 8, 16, and 24 L/h — let the system be matched to real daily demand instead of forcing a compromise in either direction.
Constant flow matters as much as the number itself: output stays predictable, so the volume available in an hour is the volume planned for.
The same flexibility runs through installation. Benchtop, wall-mounted, and built-in formats all work, so a lab short on bench space isn't excluded from the system.
iJust makes the best use of available water resources across whichever rate is selected, reducing consumption without giving up product water quality.
The closed bagtank protects produced water regardless of rate, so a higher-throughput configuration doesn't mean more water sitting exposed to airborne contamination.
